name: Athaliah
overview: Athaliah is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Jeroham, also known as Jeremoth, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:26. There are no additional notes or significant details about his life beyond this lineage. His mention is brief, focusing primarily on his genealogical placement within the tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Athaliah is a proper name meaning possibly 'y-h-v-h is exalted' or 'oldest of y-h-v-h,' indicating a theophoric element referencing the name of God. This meaning is derived from the Hebrew origin as noted in 1 Chronicles 8:26. The name was not given by God directly but carries a significant theistic connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Athaliah as the son of Jeremoth, who is also called Jeroham, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Athaliah's significance lies in his genealogical mention within the tribe of Benjamin, linking him to the lineage of Jeremoth. His record in 1 Chronicles 8:26 serves to preserve the heritage and tribal affiliations important in biblical history. While not elaborated upon with further narrative, his inclusion underscores the careful biblical attention to family lines and tribal identity.
